sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
குன்றம் எறிந்தவா குறத்தி மணாளா
குமரா குவலயம் காத்திடும் குருபரா
sections.translit:
kundRam eRindhavA kuRatthi maNALA
kumarA kuvalayam kAtthidum guruparA
sections.en: Lord Muruga split a mountain, Krauncha Giri, with a spear. He became the spouse of the tribal woman Valli. He is the younger son of the divine couple Siva and Parvathi.  He protects the universe and is a great teacher.

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
குங்கும நிற மேனியனே கும்பமுனி ப்ரியனே
குஞ்சரி மனோஹரனே குதூஹலனே
sections.translit:
kunguma niRa mEniyanE kumbhamuni priyanE
kunjari manOharaNE kudhUhalanE
sections.en: His skin is the color of vermilion (kumkum).  He is the beloved of sage Agasthiya, and the darling of Kunjari who was brought up by Indira’s elephant Airavata. He spreads joy everywhere.

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
குறுநகை தவழும் முகனே குஹனே
குட்டையில் பிறந்தவனே குப்பையில் கிடந்த
குண்டு மணியே மதிசேகரனின்
குலக்கொழுந்தே குறை நீக்கி நிறை தருவாய்
sections.translit:
kuRunagai thavazhum muganE guhanE
kuttaiyil piRandhavanE kuppaiyil kidandha
kuNdu maNiyE madhisEkaranin
kulakkozhundhE kuRai nIkki niRai tharuvAy
sections.en: Oh Lord Guha, your devotees feel elated that they have imprisoned you in the inner caves of their hearts.   Consequently, you acquired the name Guha, which means cave in Tamil.  You sport a sweet smile.  You are born in a muddy pond and yet you are like a gemstone retrieved from the rubbish.  You are an  heir of Lord Siva’s dynasty. Please remove  all our sins and blemishes and offer us a better  life.

notes: Line 1 of the pallavi refers to Lord Muruga piercing the Krauncha Mountain and demolishing it. Muruga used his spear to split the Krauncha Mountain into pieces. Per Skandapuranam in Tamil, Kraunchan was a demon related to Soorapadman and tortured devas and saints by standing as a mountain in their way, killing them and relishing it as a pastime. He had even troubled Lord Siva with his illusory tactics. Once Agasthiar had cursed him to be an inanimate mountain for eternity. Lord Muruga used the extraordinary power of his spear and split this Krauncha Mountain into two pieces and killed younger brother, Tarakasuran, as well. The details of Lord Muruga’s prowess appear in Skandapuranam. அத்தியாயம் 37: கிரௌஞ்ச மலையும் மாயாபுரிப் பட்டணமும் (பக்கம் 178 – 182) ; அத்தியாயம் 43: தாரகாசுரன் முடிவு, ஶ்ரீகந்தபுராணம், முதற் பாகம், ஆறாம் பதிப்பு ஏப்ரல் 1990, பதிப்பாசிரியர் அரு. ராமநாதன், பிரேமா பிரசுரம், 35 ஆற்காடு ரோடு, கோடம்பாக்கம், சென்னை 600024, (பக்கம்: 203 – 206). The direct verses from Thiruppugazh sing of Muruga’s prowess in breaking the Krauncha Mountain and ripping the ocean apart.
